question: Explain NestJS provider scopes and when request scope is justified.
shortAnswer: Default is singleton; request scope creates per-request instances and bubbles to dependents—use sparingly.
strongAnswer: Singleton services are created once and shared. REQUEST scope ties lifetime to a request (useful for request-bound context) but increases allocation and forces dependents request-scoped too. Prefer explicit context passing for most cases; use request scope when a true per-request collaborator is required.
followUps: How do you register a global guard with DI?
commonWrongAnswer: Every service should be request-scoped for safety.
productionRelevance: Unnecessary request scope hurts latency and memory under load.
